title: Why Air Conditioning Isn't Enough to Adapt to High Heat
paragraphs: As heat waves become more frequent and intense, air conditioning is often seen as the main way to protect people. A new study confirms that air conditioning saves thousands of lives every year, but it also shows that it cannot remove the danger completely.

The study was carried out by researchers at Yale University and published in the journal Nature Health in 2026. Instead of simply looking at whether households owned air conditioners, the team estimated how much people actually used them. They analyzed nearly 30 million death records from 3,108 counties in the continental United States between 2010 and 2020.

The researchers estimated that air conditioning prevents about 5,267 heat-related deaths in the US every year, reducing deaths caused by heat by 57%. The biggest benefits were in Florida, the Southwest and the Gulf Coast.

However, the study also revealed important limits. The benefits stopped increasing once air conditioning use reached around average levels, which means that more cooling added little extra protection. Moreover, on extremely hot days, the risk of death still rose, even in areas where air conditioners were widely used.

Cost is another problem. More than a quarter of US households say they have difficulty paying their energy bills, so some people avoid using air conditioning when they need it most. Narasimha Rao, one of the researchers, explained that some low-income households choose to "bear the heat to save money for food." In addition, using air conditioning requires a lot of energy, which can add to the emissions that cause global warming.

Because of this, the researchers say that air conditioning should be combined with other ways of reducing heat, especially by adding more trees and green spaces to cities. A separate study of more than 11,000 cities around the world, published in 2025, found that more plants could lower temperatures and reduce heat-related deaths.
The researchers also argue that heat policies should make sure people can afford to run air conditioners, not just own them.
